description: Second-order (symmetric) Trotter-Suzuki product formula. Approximates exp(-iHt) using a symmetric splitting that cancels odd-order error terms, giving quadratically better convergence than first order.
applicable_hamiltonians: Hamiltonians decomposable into a small number of terms
Systems where first-order Trotter is too inaccurate
limitations: Error still depends on nested commutator norms, but has higher-order asymptotic scaling for fixed bounded terms
The uncompressed formula has twice the Pauli exponentials per step as first order, although adjacent identical terms can be merged
Not efficient for highly non-local Hamiltonians
For very high precision, even higher-order formulas may be needed

steps.description: Number of Trotter steps. Higher values give better accuracy at the cost of more gate operations.

execution.returns: EvolutionResult with a dense unitary, framework-neutral Pauli-evolution operation sequence, or compiled reference circuit plus normalized parameters, logical and compiled costs, and provenance; evolve(...) remains compatible.

complexity.gate_count: 2 * L * n Pauli-term exponentials before compaction; adjacent identical boundary terms may be merged
complexity.circuit_depth: Backend-, connectivity-, and parallelization-dependent; OpenQEvo reports depth after compilation to its fixed logical reference basis
complexity.error_scaling: For a fixed bounded term decomposition, second-order global error is O(t^3/n^2); rigorous prefactors depend on nested commutators rather than term count alone

references.title: Generalized Trotter's formula and systematic approximants of exponential operators and inner derivations with applications to many-body problems
General theory of fractal path integrals with applications to many-body theories and statistical physics
A Theory of Trotter Error
references.authors: A. M. Childs, Y. Su, M. C. Tran, N. Wiebe, and S. Zhu
